name: Landing Page Library
description: High-converting landing page structures by product type. Every landing page is built from these proven sections in this order.

items.title: High-converting section order
items.summary: Hero -> social proof bar -> problem -> solution/benefits -> features -> how it works -> comparison -> testimonials -> pricing -> FAQ -> guarantee -> final CTA -> footer.
items.content: This is the canonical order proven across SaaS. Lead with the customer's outcome in the hero, build trust with a social proof bar, confirm the problem, present the solution and benefits, prove it with features and comparison, de-risk with testimonials + guarantee, answer objections in FAQ, and end with a final CTA that repeats the primary offer.
rules: Final CTA repeats the primary offer

items.title: Above the fold (hero)
items.summary: Within 2 seconds: headline, subheadline, one primary CTA, one trust signal. Nothing else competes.
items.content: The hero decides whether visitors stay. A single promise-focused headline, a subheadline that explains who it's for and what changes, one primary CTA button, and one trust line (users, rating, or 'No credit card'). Remove navigation clutter - minimal links.
rules: One primary CTA above the fold
One trust signal in the hero

items.title: Social proof bar
items.summary: A logo strip or key metric line directly below the hero: 'Trusted by 4,000+ teams' with recognizable logos.
items.content: Social proof immediately after the hero is highest-leverage. Use recognizable customer logos, or a metric line with a specific number. Logos build authority; numbers build credibility. Never use vague claims.

items.title: CTA copy rules
items.summary: Lead with the value the user gets, use first-person where possible ('Start my free trial'), and be specific.
items.content: Button labels should describe the outcome, not the action. Weak: 'Submit'. Strong: 'Start free trial', 'Get my proposal', 'Create my store'. Use first-person phrasing when testing shows lift. Keep CTA copy under 30 characters.
rules: First-person CTA copy when it wins tests

items.title: Headline formulas
items.summary: 1) Outcome + timeframe. 2) Who it's for + transformation. 3) Specific problem + specific fix.
items.content: Three reliable formulas: (1) 'Build your landing page in minutes, not weeks'; (2) 'The HR system for growing teams that don't want to hire an HR team'; (3) 'Stop losing deals to slow follow-up'. Quantify whenever possible.

items.title: Objection handling
items.summary: Address price, effort, and risk objections with comparison tables, FAQ, guarantee, and free trial.
items.content: The three universal objections are price, effort, and risk. Answer them directly: comparison table (price/value), 'How it works' (effort), free trial + guarantee (risk). Place answers before the pricing section.

items.title: Pricing section rules
items.summary: 3 tiers, middle tier highlighted as 'Most popular', annual toggle with visible savings, monthly price always visible.
items.content: Three tiers is the conversion sweet spot. Highlight the middle tier. Annual billing toggle showing 'Save 20%'. Avoid pricing hidden behind 'Contact sales' except for enterprise-only products. Show what's in each tier explicitly.

items.title: Guarantee & risk reversal
items.summary: A strong, specific guarantee ('30-day money-back, no questions') placed next to the final CTA.
items.content: Risk reversal is a top conversion lever. Make guarantees specific and unconditional. Show them beside the CTA, in the FAQ, and at the footer. For SaaS, 'cancel anytime' or free trial serves the same role.

items.title: Lead magnet (B2B)
items.summary: Offer a valuable free asset (template, checklist, report) in exchange for an email - email capture is above the fold for lead-gen.
items.content: For lead-generation landing pages the primary CTA may be a lead magnet. Keep the form to 2-3 fields (email + first name + company). Deliver instantly. The lead magnet must be genuinely useful to the audience.

categories.name: Patterns by Product Type
categories.description: Different structures for different business models.

items.title: SaaS landing
items.summary: Free trial CTA, product screenshot/demo in hero, feature grid, testimonials, pricing, FAQ, final CTA.
items.content: Show the product working as early as possible (screenshot, GIF or embedded demo) to reduce uncertainty. 'Start free trial' as primary CTA. Include social proof, a feature grid mapped to outcomes, testimonials with results, pricing, FAQ, final CTA.

items.title: Marketplace landing
items.summary: Split CTA for buyers and sellers, category browsing, featured listings, and platform trust signals.
items.content: Two audiences need two paths: 'Shop' and 'Start selling'. Show category tiles for browsing, featured items as proof of supply, and trust signals (payment protection, reviews, number of listings/transactions).

items.title: Consulting/service landing
items.summary: Authority-led: results, case studies, credentials, process, testimonials, and a clear contact CTA.
items.content: Services sell on authority and proof. Lead with a specific result promise, case studies with numbers, credentials and team, a clear 3-step process, testimonials, and a low-friction 'Book a call' CTA.

items.title: AI product landing
items.summary: Explain the outcome in plain language, show real output, address data privacy, offer a free trial/waitlist.
items.content: Don't lead with 'AI-powered' - lead with what it does for the user. Show real, honest outputs (avoid overpromising). Privacy and data usage must be addressed early. Free trial to reduce risk; waitlist builds scarcity for high-demand products.

items.title: Enterprise software landing
items.summary: Security/compliance badges, integrations, ROI calculator or whitepaper, and a 'Talk to sales' path.
items.content: Enterprise buyers need: security and compliance certifications, integration list, industry use cases, an ROI angle, and a human sales path. Include customer logos and proof points from similar-scale organizations.

items.title: Government platform landing
items.summary: Clarity-first: plain language, what users can do, how long it takes, eligibility, and help/accessibility links.
items.content: Government users need to complete tasks with minimal friction. Use plain language, step-by-step guidance, clear eligibility, time estimates, and prominently placed help and accessibility support.
